lab_title: Vector Mechanics and 2D Projectile Motion AR Lab
top_level_objectives: Master the visual representation of vectors in 2D space.
Understand the mathematical process of decomposing vectors into orthogonal components.
Demonstrate the independence of horizontal and vertical components in projectile motion.
Analyze how initial launch parameters influence the trajectory, range, and maximum height of a projectile.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of vector magnitude and direction using interactive arrows.
key_visuals: A 3D arrow floating in space with numerical labels for length and angle.
A coordinate grid projected on the floor.
student_actions: Drag the arrow tip to change magnitude and rotate the arrow to change direction.
Observe how the length and angle values update in real-time.

scenes.brief_purpose: Teach vector addition via the tip-to-tail method.
student_actions: Position the second arrow so its tail connects to the tip of the first arrow.
Snap the resultant vector into place to complete the triangle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize vector decomposition into x and y components.
key_visuals: A single vector and two dashed orthogonal components.
student_actions: Slide a toggle to enable/disable the display of horizontal and vertical components.
Rotate the vector to see how the component magnitudes change based on the angle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the independence of horizontal and vertical motion for a projectile.
key_visuals: Two separate markers tracking horizontal and vertical displacement.
student_actions: Watch a projectile animation where the horizontal motion is color-coded differently from the vertical motion.
Interact with a slider to scrub time forward and backward to see that horizontal velocity remains constant while vertical velocity changes.

key_visuals: A trace line showing the full parabolic path.
student_actions: Adjust sliders for launch speed and launch angle.
Fire the projectile and observe the resulting parabolic arc.

scenes.brief_purpose: Analyze range and height as a function of launch parameters.
key_visuals: Markers highlighting the peak height and impact point of the trajectory.
student_actions: Perform multiple launches at different angles to find the angle that provides maximum range.
Record the peak height values for different launch velocities.
